newsitem.title: USA: UCB mum on Southern National deal.
newsitem.headline: UCB mum on Southern National deal.

text.p: United Carolina Bancshares Corp declined comment on Sunday on reports it would be bought out by state rival Southern National Corp.

Southern National was due to announce on Monday an estimated $920 million offer for United Carolina Bancshares (UCB), according to local news reports, but a UCB spokesman dismissed the reports as rumor.
"There's no confirmation," said John McLaughlin of UCB. "What it is, is just an opportunity for UCB to repeat the standard message that UCB does not comment on rumors in the marketplace."
Southern National officials were not available for comment.
WSOC-TV and The Charlotte Observer reported the impending announcement, citing sources close to the deal who projected an offer of $38 per share, or $920 million.
UCB's stock closed up 1-1/2 at 27-1/2 on Friday. The Whiteville, N.C.-based bank had 24.3 million weighted shares outstanding at the end of the third quarter.
Winston-Salem, N.C.-based Southern National ended trading at 35-1/4 on Friday, up 5/8. It had 110.8 million weighted shares outstanding at the end of the third quarter.
The sale of UCB would mark the first of the state's midsized banks endangered by its own paucity of consumer services.

Customers of the midsize banks, for example, are not offered the huge automated teller machine network or mutual funds put forth by NationsBank Corp and First Union Corp, the banking giants of the state.

But Southern National, strengthened by its 1994 acquisition of another midsize bank, Branch Banking and Trust Co, has continued aggessively acquiring other financial institutions, including high-risk consumer loan business Regional Acceptance Corp.
